body:
For anyone wondering,

The default `values` option is: `values: {on: true, off: undefined}`. Which means: when "on", refine the attribute with `true` (boolean). When off, refine with `undefined` => show both true and false values.

So if you do not provide the `values` option, when the widget initializes, we will not refine on anything.

Let's say you have a "free shipping" toggle, it will show you by default both free and not free shipping. When you activate it, it will only show free shipping articles.

Given your context, this might not be what you want, you might for instance want to refine with `false` on initialization and when off (example: hide by default the archived products, let the user show them only)

To do so, pass `values: {on: true, off: false}`. But as soon as you do so, you will always have the default toggle "false" showing in the current refined values widgets. Because we did refine on the attribute with `false`.

This is why @davidpike7, in your example, it shows the filter inside the current refined values by default: this is the off value.
1. How could we make this more clear?
2. Is this in the end what you want? Maybe you want the default behavior (true/undefined)
3. Maybe you would want a "doNotRefineOnInit" option? But for users this would be not accurate.

Thanks again for being an awesome user of instantsearch.js and to give us feedback!
